key_insight: Dielectric measurements reveal a shift from collective relaxation to localized orientational defects during AESO curing, while a machine learning potential captures the defects’ rotational energy profiles.
engineering_relevance: Connecting rotational barriers to dielectric response could help interpret cure monitoring in bio-based polymer networks.
method: Measure dielectric permittivity at 500–5000 Hz during intermittent UV curing of an AESO:VDM mixture.
Analyze relaxation dynamics using sliding-window Shannon entropy and Grassberger–Procaccia correlation integrals.
Benchmark MACE-OFF23 relaxed dihedral scans of five AESO rotational modes against DFT.
evidence_signal: MACE matches DFT profile shapes with Pearson r = 0.95–0.98 and preserves the rotational-barrier hierarchy; Arrhenius estimates place acrylate rotations closest to the dielectric measurement window.
watch_item: MACE underestimates barrier heights by 3–20%, and fragment-based scans may not capture constraints imposed by the cured network.
paper_title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
